scope: Calibration corpus of REAL works, paraphrased from published reviews, curatorial texts and artist/venue pages read via scrapling (April 2024 - Oct 2026 coverage): 13th Berlin Biennale 2025, 15th (2024) and 16th (2026, opened 5 Sept 2026) Gwangju Biennale, 18th Istanbul Biennial 2025, 17th Lyon Biennale 2024, Manifesta 15 Barcelona 2024, Liverpool Biennial 2025, Taipei Biennial 2025 (title: Whispers on the Horizon, not 'Small World'), 15th Shanghai Biennale 2025, Art Basel Unlimited 2025. Unknown fields are null. Facts taken only from the page cited in each record's source (a few details marked 'reported' came from search summaries).

exhibitions.name: 13th Berlin Biennale for Contemporary Art
exhibitions.artistic_director: Zasha Colah (curator; Valentina Viviani assistant curator)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Urban foxes seen in Berlin are the starting image for 'fugitivity': art that slips past repressive systems. The title reads as a note or instruction passed to the viewer, who then receives 'cultural evidence'.
sections: Encounters series (talks, tribunals, walks, comedy nights, unannounced 'fugitive acts')
Sister organizations: ERIAC, Filmrauschpalast Moabit, SİNEMA TRANSTOPIA, Sophiensæle
critic_notes: Artists list was held back until opening day; critics read this as fear of another documenta fifteen row, and read the whole show as evasive about Gaza.
Several critics saw an unspoken 'politics of omission' as the organising idea; one found it clever, others found it cowardly or euphemistic.
Myanmar protest art (Htein Lin, Chaw Ei Thein, Panties for Peace, Nge Nom, Sawangwongse Yawnghwe) became the de facto spine of the show.
Many works sit as small samples of larger practices; one critic compared the walk to channel-flipping on satellite radio, with wall text doing most of the work.
Hung tightly and with minimal context, mostly sculpture and installation; Lehrter Straße courthouse section called rough but stronger than the polished KW floor.
Strongest-praised items: Htein Lin's The Fly, Jane Jin Kaisen's videos of Jeju sea divers, Fredj Moussa's 16mm Decameron film, Vikrant Bhise's mural, Panties for Peace.
Frieze judged it 'belated': the political ground in Berlin moved before the opening.

exhibitions.name: 15th Gwangju Biennale - PANSORI: A Soundscape of the 21st Century
exhibitions.artistic_director: Nicolas Bourriaud (with Sophia Park, Kuralai Abdukhalikova, Barbara Lagié)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Pansori is the Korean sung-storytelling form (singer plus drummer); the curators gloss pan as public space and sori as voice or noise, so 'the voice of the subalterns'. The show is pitched as an opera you can walk into, with each landscape also a soundscape.
sections: Gwangju Biennale Pavilion (31 national and institutional pavilions)
critic_notes: Frieze: the sound theme is only a vague motif; sound works are walled into separate rooms; best are the big phantasmagorical set-like installations (Bondi, Hooper Schneider, Park, Shust, Leatherbury).
ArtReview: 'disconcertingly vague'; wall texts stretch pansori to mean everything; works carry almost no labels so viewers read them by form alone.
e-flux: the section texts are so broad they cannot be applied; the satellite single-artist rooms in Yangnim-dong work better than the 'opera'.
Art Newspaper: subtler on Gwangju's political history than earlier editions; opening hall is a literal black box tunnel then a wrecked office.
Recurring look: apocalyptic ruin sculpture, dioramas of fake landscape, sand, pipes, plastic, mirrors, soft-sculpted bodies, slow-motion video.

exhibitions.name: 16th Gwangju Biennale - You Must Change Your Life
exhibitions.artistic_director: Ho Tzu Nyen (with Che Kyongfa, Park Gahee, Brian Kuan Wood)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: The last line of Rilke's 1908 poem 'Archaic Torso of Apollo', in which a broken statue commands the viewer to change; critics add Sloterdijk's book of the same title and the idea of self-help as a genre. Opened 5 Sept 2026, so reviews are only weeks old.
critic_notes: Fewest artists since 1995 and one building; artists recur across all five galleries (Sasaki Ken with 50-60 paintings, Goldin+Senneby, Rossella Biscotti, Nina Canell, Rim Dong Sik).
Kunstkritikk: sincere, subdued, organic; repetition is the real method (Sloterdijk's anthropotechnics) but Sasaki and the unattributed Jeju volcanic rocks are overused.
Frieze: didactic maxim opens each room; best works are tender, bodily, personal (Amanda Heng, Sohrab Hura, Maya Watanabe).
Run-up news: Taiwan pavilion naming row, China withdrew its pavilion; foundation president apologised.
Volcanic rocks from Jeju are listed as participants on equal footing with human artists.

exhibitions.name: 18th Istanbul Biennial - The Three-Legged Cat
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Istanbul's street cats as emblems of survival; a three-legged cat still jumps and plays, so loss becomes a way to build a new balance. The biennial also runs in three 'legs' over 2025-2027 (exhibition, academy, closing exhibitions).
sections: First leg: exhibition 20 Sept - 23 Nov 2025 across 8 venues (Galata Greek School, Zihni Han, Elhamra Han, Muradiye Han, Galeri 77, Former Cone Factory, Meclis-i Mebusan 35, Garden of the Former French Orphanage)
critic_notes: Frieze: concise, matter-of-fact, no orchestral swell; strong run of video; flat painting everywhere; renovated venues feel emotionally inert.
Text zur Kunst: at least a dozen artists are repeat biennial names; many installations carry an 'informational-allegorical apparatus' and a moral at the end like a fable.
e-flux: play is the buried theme (swings, hopscotch, game consoles) yet attendants stop visitors using them.
Several works address Gaza and Palestine directly; critics note the show is silent on Turkey's own histories.
Organisational background: the previous curator selection scandal and postponement.

exhibitions.name: 17th Lyon Biennale - Les voix des fleuves / Crossing the water
exhibitions.title_metaphor: The confluence of the Rhône and Saône as a picture of human encounter; rivers carry voices and stories, and water must be crossed to reach the Other. Literary touchstones named in the text: Sally Rooney and Sylvia Plath.
sections: Les Grandes Locos (former rail workshops, flagship)
Cité internationale de la Gastronomie - Grand Hôtel-Dieu (former hospital)
critic_notes: ArtReview: reads like a safe ChatGPT biennial theme; many French and Beaux-Arts de Paris names; well-intentioned but adrift in vague metaphor; compassion fatigue.
Frieze: relationships among artists and curator are the real theme; textile, sound and video installations carry the former rail depot.
Canvas: no visible curatorial ego, big monumental installations of a kind other biennials avoid; mood is mischievous.
ArtNews: nine standouts include a neon repair map, giant seesaw, 50 whistling pressure cookers, cave-singing video with resonance paintings.

exhibitions.name: Manifesta 15 Barcelona Metropolitana
exhibitions.city: Barcelona (Sant Adrià de Besòs and 12 municipalities)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: A nomadic European biennial that leaves the tourist centre for the industrial and suburban belt; three themes name its 'hubs'. A speculative 'regenerative' reading of art as cure for a damaged region.
sections: Imagining Futures (Tres Xemeneies power station, Sant Adrià de Besòs)
Balancing Conflicts (Casa Gomis near the airport and others)
Cure and Care (Monastery of Sant Cugat and others)
Former Gustavo Gili publishing house (archive shows)
critic_notes: ArtReview: art becomes an afterthought; 'healing' is a slippery catchall; spread too thin over a huge region; old industrial venues give little spectacle.
Kunstkritikk: the three-chimney power station outshines the rest and works as the de facto main show.
Frieze: standouts are wind, braided hair, chalk blackboards, a monastery shrine of salt and glass.

exhibitions.name: Liverpool Biennial 2025 - BEDROCK
exhibitions.title_metaphor: The red and yellow sandstone under Liverpool, used as a figure for other foundations: colonialism, migration, family, music, football, religion. Three programme weekends map to civic and colonial history, family, geology and time.
critic_notes: Hyperallergic: fragmented over 14 venues plus outdoor works, no anchor venue, few Liverpool-connected artists; many works too weak or speculative for the theme.
Wallpaper: shines when works meet unexpected city contexts (shopfronts, pavements, cathedral).
Earth materials recur: clay, barley, soil.

exhibitions.name: Taipei Biennial 2025 - Whispers on the Horizon
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Yearning: a private, percolating longing for something never fully touched. Three 'lodestar' objects from Taiwanese culture (a puppet from The Puppetmaster, a diary from a Chen Yingzhen story, a bicycle from The Stolen Bicycle) recur as trios of old museum photographs.
sections: Taipei Fine Arts Museum, stacked white-cube floors
Historic works from the museum collection and National Palace Museum interleaved
critic_notes: ArtReview: layered manifesto and overembedded conceits not needed; the works are strong and 'chatter' alone; curiously erotic show.
Frieze: playful and gently apolitical; best when using the museum's own holdings.
Reported artist count differs by source (54 vs 72).

exhibitions.name: 15th Shanghai Biennale - Does the flower hear the bee?
exhibitions.artistic_director: Kitty Scott (chief curator; Daisy Desrosiers, Xue Tan co-curators)
exhibitions.title_metaphor: Scientific finding that flowers sense the sound of bee wings and make sweeter nectar in response; used to ask how human and nonhuman intelligences perceive each other. Exhibition design by all(zone) is a 'garden-like landscape' without thematic zones.
sections: Power Station of Art atrium and floors
City Projects: Jia Yuan Hai Art Museum, VILLA tbh, Shanghai Botanical Garden Penjing Garden, klee klee & friends
critic_notes: ArtReview: strong sign-and-symbol theme; the fake flower atrium and complimentary honey sachet at the door feel like branding; wall texts often quote the artist; 'meaning and meaninglessness' are close.
ArtAsiaPacific: attunement is not new thinking; wayfinding by sound and scent left viewers disoriented and reliant on text.

exhibitions.name: Art Basel Unlimited 2025
exhibitions.title_metaphor: A hall (172,000 sq ft) for works too big for a booth: monumental installations, immersive video and live performance, sold by galleries.
critic_notes: Mix of reactivated historic works (Kippenberger, Merz, Kusama, Gonzalez-Torres, Andre) and new commissions; many textile, mirror, light and screen-wall works.

works.title: Artists' Street
works.medium_line: hand-stitched textile sculptures; shown with Self-Portrait as Stuffed Doll, 2004-08
works.what_you_see: A street of small soft models: hand-stitched fabric buildings and figures, each staging a protest action by Myanmar artists, from the 1996 student marches through the 2007 Saffron Revolution to the years after the 2021 coup. A stuffed-doll self-portrait from 2004-08 is shown among them at KW.
claims: Together the pieces form a layered record of decades of resistance.
Each piece acts as embodied memory of a protest the artist saw or heard about.
works.photo_notes: Spike photo shows soft figures and houses at KW next to Panties for Peace emblems and Exterra XX performance objects.

works.title: Las montañas saben lo que hicieron [The mountains know what they did]
works.medium_line: retablos (folk altars), banners; also Retablo para cargar en la espalda, 2025; Retablos para compartir
works.what_you_see: Bright, densely illustrated folk altars on poles. Some are made to be carried on the back or shared in marches against lithium mining concessions in the Argentina-Chile-Bolivia region. In the Hamburger Bahnhof hall they stand beside patterned sarongs and large drawings, so the room reads like a procession paused in a museum. One banner says the colonizer is naked.
nonvisual: performance: carried retablos used in protest marches; an Encounter on 15 June 2025 at the museum
claims: Uses state and colonial symbols to mock the nation state.
Criticises cultural mixing that ignores Indigenous cosmology and sacred land.
references: Emperor's New Clothes (banner: the colonizer is naked)
works.photo_notes: Spike photo: altars, Larissa Araz drawings and Zamthingla Ruivah Shimray sarongs hung together in one large hall.

works.title: Die Komödie!
works.medium_line: installation: reprinted pamphlets, fans, annotated maps, neon sign, toy soldiers
works.what_you_see: Rooms of the former Moabit court where Karl Liebknecht stood trial in 1916. In one, red reprinted pamphlets are whipped around by large fans; in another, wall maps are covered with notes on global finance, agribusiness, tech and pharma. A pen, toy soldiers and a neon sign for communism sit more quietly.
nonvisual: sound: fan noise implied by the moving pamphlets (not described in sources)
claims: Echoes Liebknecht calling his trial a comedy.
Lists the large powers workers must unite against.
works.photo_notes: Frieze caption shows red leaflets in mid-air in a high court room.

works.title: The Fly
works.medium_line: video of a performance first made in prison (restaged 2008)
works.what_you_see: A low-fi film of a naked man bound to a chair with hands behind his back, snapping at an imaginary fly. He catches and eats it, then convulses, then turns and asks the viewer why they stay silent. Prison paintings by the same artist hang in the courthouse venue.
nonvisual: performance: the filmed act is a restaging of a prison ritual
claims: The curator treats his courtroom laughter as the biennial's central metaphor for defiance.
works.photo_notes: Frieze still: grainy single figure in a chair, bare room.

works.title: The Ditch
works.medium_line: dug ground installation
works.what_you_see: A modest hole dug into the ground at the back of the KW building, with almost no objects around it. The wall text carries the story: the artist launched a civil disobedience movement, was chased by military vehicles and was taken in by neighbours. A critic found the hole added nothing to what the label already said.
claims: Presented as an example of fugitivity and survival.
works.photo_notes: Spike photo: a plain cut in the ground, almost no objects.

works.venue_room: Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall, Gallery 1-2 (Feedback Effect)
works.title: Não existe mais lugar neste lugar [There Is No More Place in This Place]
works.medium_line: carpet, metal, foam, lamps
works.dimensions: 796 x 1,101 x 230 cm (space design: Flora Simon Gurgel)
works.what_you_see: You walk out of a blacked-out sound tunnel into a silent, empty, carpeted office-type room under bright light. The ceiling tiles hang loose and out of line as if after a quake. On a rainy day the dark industrial carpet picks up mud from visitors' shoes, which adds to the sense of damage.
nonvisual: sound: bleed from the preceding noise tunnel
claims: Sets a sensory jolt at the start of the show.
works.photo_notes: ArtReview photo: wide pale room, drooping ceiling grid.

works.title: LYSIS FIELD
works.medium_line: kinetic sand craters, freshwater ecosystem, fabricated junk waterfall, copper-electroplated vegetation, cultivated crystallisations, scavenged objects and local waste, decomposed granite ground cover
works.what_you_see: A room-filling fake landscape: crater-like sand pits where small metal spheres draw patterns on their own, a junk waterfall, plants plated in copper, crystals grown on found waste from Gwangju. Odd composite creatures and small robots seem to live in it. A slowed pop ballad from the neighbouring video drifts over it.
nonvisual: sound: slowed 1983 pop ballad from a nearby video bleeds in
claims: Shows the moment of 'lysis' when a harmful substance breaks down and regains ecological value.
Offers a speculative picture of a post-Anthropocene ecosystem.
works.photo_notes: Art Newspaper photo: dense, dark, teeming set-like landscape.

works.title: objects of the wind
works.medium_line: installation; mirrors, photographs, stainless steel shelf, props
works.what_you_see: A long horizontal landscape of lit makeup mirrors with bulb frames, photographs of pungmul drumming, and a stainless steel shelf holding paperbacks, empty tea cups, nurses' caps, feather headdresses and gongs. It reads as a memorial display.
claims: Memorial to Korean nurses who worked in West German hospitals in the 1960s-70s.
Reinterprets Korean folklore through a mother-migrant story.
works.photo_notes: Artnet photo: a long mirror with bulbs on top and sides, objects on a bench.

works.title: Valence
works.medium_line: ten modular kinetic sculptures with silicone rubber, pneumatic system, sound composition
works.what_you_see: In a dim room, ten shelf-like modules each hold a white pillowy silicone shape modelled on a scan of the artist's brain. A metal rod prods each in rhythm; the soft form dents and swells and makes sounds like an MRI machine.
nonvisual: sound: composition that drives the pneumatic pokes; MRI-like clicks and thuds
claims: Links pansori to free will and collective action.
Questions the relation between human and machine.
works.photo_notes: Artnet photo: dim room, shelves each holding a white object.

works.title: Crying Uncle's Room
works.medium_line: sculptural installation; plastic encasings, circuit-board-like panels, polystyrene trays
works.what_you_see: Body parts, arms, legs and intestines, wrapped in plastic and packed onto big circuit-board shapes or butcher-shop style white trays. Some rise suspended in a heap. You cannot tell flesh from mannequin.
claims: Reads as a horror show; the body feels alienated from itself.
works.photo_notes: ArtReview describes dense pile of limbs; no photo detail.

works.title: Resin Pond
works.medium_line: about two tonnes of pine resin
works.what_you_see: First thing you meet in the show: about two tonnes of glowing golden pine resin poured across the floor like a river, just beyond the Rilke poem printed on a clear panel at the entrance.
claims: Resin both heals a tree wound and can be turned into aviation fuel: healing tipping into harm.
Rooted in one artist's experience of multiple sclerosis.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: amber resin spreading across a museum floor (ARTnews caption dates it 2006; Kunstkritikk dates it 2026).

works.title: Not Exactly BPM (Variation Rrose)
works.medium_line: multi-channel sound, transparent vinyl inflatables, centrifugal blowers, microcontroller, acrylic, steel and wood
works.what_you_see: A maze of clear vinyl inflatables that swell and collapse under amber and white neon strips, with club music. It fills the last gallery and can be entered from the plaza without a ticket.
nonvisual: sound: original techno composition by Rrose
claims: A deconstructed club that closes the journey with air and breath.
works.photo_notes: Frieze main image: amber-lit inflatables in a large hall.

works.artist_born: (Kwon: sound and performance artist; Park: Seoul-based media artist)
works.title: Bullim (Augmentation)
works.medium_line: instruments and acoustic devices cast from donated scrap metal
works.what_you_see: Instruments and sound devices melted down from metal objects donated by residents of Gwangju and South Jeolla. They were played in a live opening performance.
nonvisual: performance: live set at the opening
claims: Reinterprets the shamanic ritual of soegeollip, when a novice shaman collects scrap metal door to door.
works.photo_notes: No installation photo described.

works.title: Sagami River (one of 50-60 works; also Sneakers, 2010; Switch, 2009; Cat [Shiitake], 2023)
works.medium_line: oil on canvas
works.what_you_see: Neutral, precise paintings of everyday things: sneakers, a light switch, tea towels, tennis balls, a fire extinguisher, a cat. They are hung in grids and repeat through every gallery as a guide.
claims: Wall text frames the series as a long questioning of yoga, Western-style painting.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: grid hang of small canvases beside a ping-pong table.

works.venue_room: Garden of the Former French Orphanage
works.title: Red Navigapparate
works.medium_line: installation; red pipe, red pallet jack, marble pedestal, red barrels with trees
works.what_you_see: A gravel courtyard cut in two by a narrow water channel. On one side about a hundred olive, citrus and nut trees stand in red barrels on pallets. On the other a red pallet jack rests on a marble block. A red pipe runs in the channel.
claims: Distils food, transport and border into one scene about frozen movement.
works.photo_notes: Text zur Kunst image: red barrels on pallets in a ruined garden.

works.title: A nest is a fruit that swells
works.medium_line: cotton fabric, dye pigments, cords, ropes, plaster and gauze, cans, wall paint, avocado peels, clay, burlap, felt rugs, bleach, cement, bells, recycled plastic containers, stones, tree branches
works.what_you_see: A walk-in room draped with every sort of cloth, with portraits and motifs on every surface. One palm pushes out of a column and presses on the floor like a limb.
claims: Gives a lived-in, play-like space.
works.photo_notes: E-flux photo: dense layered cloth room.

works.title: Chasing the Sun
works.medium_line: sandboxes, stars, sun, wire cars, olive trees, clouds, seesaw, swing sets, sailboat, toy horse
works.what_you_see: A playground on a roof terrace with a view of the Princes' Islands: three wooden swings, a hopscotch, a see-saw, a sandpit and a huge wooden toy horse. Guards allow only the swings. A shelf shows a Molotov, a toy rifle and a slingshot.
claims: Plays on the difference between play and institutional control.
works.photo_notes: E-flux photo: terrace playground in the open air.

works.title: Working Class
works.medium_line: cardboard
works.what_you_see: Hollow cardboard limbs, head and hammer of a 1973 workers' monument hang from the ceiling above mirrored pools, so the parts double and break. A video shows an actor as the sculptor repeatedly repairing it.
claims: The scattered body stands for the break-up of labour movements.
works.photo_notes: E-flux photo: pale cardboard limbs hanging.

works.title: A Horn That Swallows Songs
works.medium_line: two-room installation; ultrasonic speakers, floor transducers, subwoofers, polished metal structure, four screens, repurposed factory machinery
works.what_you_see: Two connected rooms echo a Turkish delight (lokum) factory floor. In the first, a polished metal structure holds four video screens with footage and interviews from factory visits; one screen carries a single voice read from interview transcripts. In the second, a sculpture made from reused factory machinery forms a horn-like vent, like those used for halva. Low-frequency vibrations from speakers, floor transducers and subwoofers pass through the floor into the visitor's body.
nonvisual: sound: low-frequency vibrations through the floor into the body
claims: Exposes the invisible labour of women in lokum factories.
Shows the gap between workers' reality and management's tidy account.
works.photo_notes: Press images by Sahir Ugur Eren exist; no description in the source read.

works.venue_room: Les Grandes Locos (underground and upper gallery)
works.title: Resonance Project: The Cave
works.medium_line: eight-screen video installation; Resonance Paintings
works.what_you_see: Two-floor installation: eight screens switch on and off, each showing a singer with a lamp inside a Palaeolithic cave. Below, paintings made by pouring cave pigment on canvases laid over speakers so sound shapes the pigment.
nonvisual: sound: eight a cappella voices in polyphony
claims: Joins singers into one polyphony.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: abstract paintings in an underground room.

works.venue_room: Cité internationale de la Gastronomie - Grand Hôtel-Dieu
works.title: El Brujo Disease Thrower
works.medium_line: steel gong, cotton, glue mixture, plastic, loofah, oil on tin, objects collected from a ritual retracing the artist's migration route
works.what_you_see: A sound sculpture in a former hospital, assembled from a steel gong, cotton, glue mixture, plastic, loofah and oil-on-tin pieces plus objects gathered on a ritual that retraced the artist's own migration route. It is shown with other Disease Throwers (such as Pierna de Serpiente, 2023) and a weaving titled Pour Les Ancêtres.
claims: Presented as healing instruments.
works.photo_notes: Lyon site lists photo credit Jair Lanes; no description.

works.venue_room: Cité internationale de la Gastronomie - former apothecary
works.title: Violette Cristal
works.medium_line: wax sculpture inlaid with amethyst fragments and violet-flavoured candies
works.what_you_see: A giant open violet carved in wax stands among old earthenware pots and wooden cabinets, with amethyst chips and candies catching the light. You smell it.
claims: Perfume ties memory to seduction.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: violet in a room with blue-and-white pots.

works.title: Marmites enragées [Raging Cookers]
works.medium_line: about 50 modified pressure cookers
works.what_you_see: Around fifty ordinary pressure cookers are gathered in the old rail workshops and fitted so they let off steam in the tune of the socialist anthem The Internationale. The mass of steel pots reads as an uprising of kitchen objects in a space that once housed workers' struggles.
claims: Ridicules the idea that women should stay in the kitchen.
Points to the long history and latent possibility of a united revolt.
references: labour history of the Grandes Locos
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: massed cookers.

works.title: The Majority of Accent
works.medium_line: painting on textile, embroidery and seeds on printed fabric
works.what_you_see: A large textile print of a quarry, 4.8 by 2.9 metres, with biomorphic figures painted and embroidered over it and seeds worked in. Images of labour organising recall the rail hangar's past. Sacks that are printed, painted and embroidered hide speakers that play recorded interviews with former workers.
claims: Recalls the venue's labour history.
works.photo_notes: Frieze main image: large patterned cloth.

works.title: Prehension
works.medium_line: 22 lengths of industrial white linen; open windows
works.what_you_see: Twenty-two industrial lengths of white linen cascade from the ceiling of the top floor of the old power station. Window panes were removed so sea wind makes them billow, and the movement is visible from outside, a few metres from the coast. The cloth is expected to pull, stain and tear over the run.
claims: Wind is the art; the fabric will tear.
works.photo_notes: Frieze main image: pale cloth in a concrete hall.

works.title: Yield
works.medium_line: root-woven carpet with grass; soil
works.what_you_see: An organic, earth-scented 'rug' made of manipulated plant roots in mirrored spine-like patterns on the front and dense grass growing on the back. It hangs like a huge tongue from the ceiling down to the floor on the first floor of the turbine hall.
claims: Spine motif refers to Gaudí and a slave-trade patron.
works.photo_notes: Kunstkritikk shows tall vertical rug.

works.title: Dïà s p o r a
works.medium_line: black synthetic braiding hair, soil, rice plants
works.what_you_see: A web of black braided hair fills a former textile factory; visitors duck under until it is too low, and knee-high rice sprouts from soil mounds. It was braided by local women over two weeks.
claims: Recalls enslaved women hiding seeds in braids.
works.photo_notes: Frieze shows dense black web.

works.title: Un Intruso (uninvited, into chaos)
works.medium_line: shack of discarded construction materials, iron bed, coal stove
works.what_you_see: A rough shack built from local scrap outside the power plant; inside only an iron bed frame and a small coal stove, with a window framing the chimneys.
works.photo_notes: No photo detail.

works.title: Temple du soin [Temple of Care]
works.medium_line: water-based mixed-media installation: carpet tapestries, salt, glass fountains, clay bowls
works.what_you_see: Three midnight-blue carpets hang in the cloister, each with a fertile female form; white salt crystals cover the floor around small glass fountains with masked heads; clay bowls hold dried herbs.
claims: Evokes a divine maternal cloister.
works.photo_notes: Frieze photo: blue hangings in stone room.

works.title: Away Terrace (Us and Them)
works.medium_line: sculptural and sonic installation; bricks made of clay and barley straw, pigments, timber, 10-channel audio
works.what_you_see: A rough football terrace stands in a warehouse, built from dense blocks of clay and barley straw and timber. Ten channels of audio mimic the buzz of a match crowd, with a trance-like pulse. Critics split: one called it a primal stadium, another sprawling but drab. It is shown beside clay sculptures by another artist.
claims: Speaks to a need for belonging and the social cost of exclusion.
works.photo_notes: Frieze photo: earth-block stand.

works.title: Underground Flourishings
works.medium_line: more than 100 wall-mounted clay sculptures using clay from the River Mersey; drawings and moving image
works.what_you_see: A shrine-like wall of handmade clay sculptures, reported as over a hundred, with plant and animal motifs from Peruvian pre-Columbian knowledge, made from clay dug from the River Mersey. It shares the 20 Jordan Street warehouse with a football-terrace installation. Drawings and moving image sit alongside.
claims: Asks us to reflect on the damage of treating ecosystems as natural resources.
works.photo_notes: Phileas gives installation photos.

works.title: Where Am I Now?
works.medium_line: crocheted steel with embroidery
works.what_you_see: A veil of crocheted steel hangs from a pointed arch inside Liverpool Cathedral, embroidered with a scene of local birds carrying souls skywards. It echoes the building's architecture and the birds that nest nearby.
claims: Described by a critic as refreshingly sincere.
works.photo_notes: Frieze photo: pale veil under a Gothic arch.

works.title: Muly'Ato Lima [All in one boat]
works.medium_line: aluminium passports, chairs, jerry cans, woven mat
works.what_you_see: Aluminium passports, chairs, jerry cans and a woven mat are set out at Bluecoat as a large installation on African migration. A related earlier work, No Hurry (2020), sits in a menswear shop display: aluminium trainers blended into the shelves. The artist collected aluminium as a child to trade for toys.
claims: Reflects African migration and the 'all in one boat' idea.
works.photo_notes: Hyperallergic photo: passports and chairs on a mat; Wallpaper photo of trainers in a shop.

works.venue_room: Entrance gallery, Taipei Fine Arts Museum
works.title: Cizania
works.medium_line: wood, recycled plywood
works.what_you_see: A giant root ball of scrap plywood spreads across the entrance gallery as if the floorboards had torn up and regrown. One part is cut off by a floor-to-ceiling window and teeters outside on stilts like a shipwreck, facing its other half.
claims: Critic reads it as growth, renewal, repair or a 'whisper on the horizon'.
works.photo_notes: ArtReview photo: huge wooden mass.

works.title: Sock series (incl. The Bloom That Holds Her Shadow)
works.medium_line: videos and mixed media; socks bought from online fetishists
works.what_you_see: Resin feet and worn socks are staged as personified sculptures, with videos of fetish content bought by the artist playing on a loop and the chats that led to each purchase. On screen socks are peeled off and toes wiggle through. Visitors are invited to look over a shoulder.
claims: Gently mocks the voyeurism of exhibition-goers and social media.
works.photo_notes: Berlinartlink: feet and screens on a table.

works.title: Aniconism as Figuration Urgency (Post-Scriptum)
works.medium_line: laser-cut iron, spice powders; Thala marble
works.what_you_see: A curved calligraphic sculpture cut from iron hangs over low piles of coloured spice powders, with inscribed marble stones laid nearby that retrace the path to a family burial ground in Tunisia. The room smells of spice.
claims: Arouses senses to link to loss and cultural memory.
works.photo_notes: Berlinartlink image.

works.title: Still My Eyes Water
works.medium_line: natural fabrics, pottery, mixed media
works.what_you_see: A large bouquet of fabric flowers, all native to Palestine, spreads in every direction on a table in a dark room. It is one of the first things on the main floor.
claims: Express longing for a place that may not return in the same form.
works.photo_notes: Berlinartlink image.

works.title: Recipients
works.medium_line: three-channel video installation
works.what_you_see: Three screens show the artist's elderly mother tending a crowded plant collection on her Tokyo balcony, then showing her daughter analogue slides of old flowers. The images link soil, hands and slides.
claims: Quiet study of mutual care and interspecies relations.
references: Chen Chin Out in the Fields (1934)
works.photo_notes: ArtReview photo.

works.title: Phantom Forest
works.medium_line: synthetic flowers
works.what_you_see: In the big atrium of a former coal-fired power plant, clouds of yellow synthetic flowers float with no trunks or roots, and the same flowers lie in drifts on the floor like fallen leaves. Families gather under them to take photos.
claims: Critic reads fake nature as advertising and a selfie spot.
works.photo_notes: Biennial Association photo.

works.title: How to Carve a Sculpture
works.medium_line: wood gnawed by beavers; CNC copies
works.what_you_see: Slim wooden forms gnawed by beavers from Japanese zoos are shown beside human-size totems that copy them using CNC routers. The beaver counts as the artist, the machine as copyist.
claims: Beavers become artists.
works.photo_notes: ArtReview text.

works.title: Dust
works.medium_line: sawdust, gravel, sand, nylon thread
works.what_you_see: Sawdust, gravel, sand, nylon thread and other debris from a furniture factory in Wuhan are arranged into a floating, striped cloud shape. The label calls the factory a harsh and inhuman workplace.
claims: Stands as a riposte to the flower garden at the entrance.
works.photo_notes: Text only.

works.title: To Make Smoke
works.medium_line: charcoal smudges on wall
works.what_you_see: A wall carries smudges of charcoal from burning sage and sweetgrass in ceremony, applied so lightly it nearly vanishes. The mark sits between something and nothing.
claims: Disrupts the white cube of the museum.
works.photo_notes: Text only.

works.title: Danse Macabre
works.medium_line: truss structure, wool and horsehair tendrils, vintage furniture legs
works.what_you_see: A huge twisting creature of tendrils made from salvaged horsehair and raw wool hangs from a truss above the hall, with vintage furniture legs among the tangle. Reported as about ten metres high.
claims: Explores life and death, human and non-human, attraction and repulsion.
works.photo_notes: Art Basel photo.

works.title: The Voyage - A March to Utopia
works.medium_line: 80-piece installation
works.what_you_see: An 80-piece procession runs from the entrance to the exit of the hall, led by a discarded, repaired scooter called the Leader. It is followed by pickaxes, mannequins, prosthetics, pumping machines, and works like a red steamroller and a coffee-making operating table.
claims: A journey to utopia; the patched toy stands for resilience.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo.

works.title: Os Comedores de Terra / The Earth Eaters
works.medium_line: double-sided installation
works.what_you_see: A double-sided piece. The front is a panoramic landscape painting about 54 feet wide that shows scars of logging and slash-and-burn. It is mounted on wooden scaffolding that carries giant papier-mâché gems in many colours.
claims: The end is near, but there is beauty in natural disasters (artist remark).
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo.

works.title: sapphire cinnamon viper fairy
works.medium_line: 200 looping videos on 50 screens
works.what_you_see: Two hundred looping videos on 50 screens in a staggered salon-style hang: people dancing, people looking at screens. Begun in 2007 and edited until 2023 from found footage.
claims: Invites reflection on how fast online content is consumed.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo.

works.title: House of Hope Archives
works.medium_line: five slide projectors, 400 photographs
works.what_you_see: In a basement under a clanking, glowing sound installation by another artist, five slide projectors cycle through about 400 photographs credited to the artist's parents. The room is dark and apart from the main hall; a critic found it a better home for the work than the main show.
nonvisual: sound: clanking from the installation on the floor above
claims: Presented as an archive carried across generations.
works.photo_notes: E-flux photo: projectors on stands and light on a wall.

works.title: Stock Weather III
works.medium_line: installation: stock-market-controlled fans, miniature desert, camera, curved monitors
works.what_you_see: Fans driven by live stock-market data blow wind over a small model desert. A camera films the scene and shows it on curved monitors, while a rotating arm sweeps like a clock. The landscape stays stuck in twilight.
nonvisual: sound: fans and machine hum (not described)
claims: Connects the man-made global economy with weather.
Hints at the game-like nature of economics and a bleak future.
references: fluid dynamics of wind and water
works.photo_notes: Artnet photo of the work in the biennale hall.

works.title: XENON PALACE CHAMPIONSHIP
works.medium_line: interactive film, video game, PVC inflatable seating, custom-made hookah-handle controllers, automotive silicone intake hoses
works.what_you_see: A game station for several players: inflatable PVC seats like a hookah lounge, controllers shaped like shisha handles and connected by silicone hoses, and a platform game on screen. Visitors sit and play.
claims: Turns a platform game into a refuge from racialised daily indignity.
works.photo_notes: E-flux photo: inflatable seats in a semicircle.

works.title: Be Our Guest
works.medium_line: mixed-media installation: printed mattresses, second-hand lamps and tables, wall mind map, lounge music
works.what_you_see: A room styled like a short-let apartment: mattresses on the floor printed with 16 interview accounts from French hospitality workers (taken from 29 interviews) in the sans-serif font TripAdvisor uses, mismatched second-hand lamps and tables, a bright orange mind map of her research across the wall, and lounge-like background music.
claims: Questions the gap between giving welcome and selling hospitality.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo: word map on wall with mattresses and lamps.

works.title: Mortier Fati – Lignes de lumière
works.medium_line: neon lights tracing repairs on the ceiling
works.what_you_see: Look up: on the vaulted ceiling of the old rail hangar, thin neon lines trace the mortar patches where stonemasons filled cracks, so the repairs read as a glowing, almost unreadable script.
claims: Celebrates the beauty of imperfections and repair.
works.photo_notes: ArtReview photo: ceiling grid with glowing lines.

works.venue_room: Taipei Fine Arts Museum, second floor
works.title: K'obomanik (Gratitude for everything that lights up and turns off before our eyes)
works.medium_line: stones, rope, soil, ceramics, water and digital screens
works.what_you_see: Heavy stones hang in gauzy curtain cocoons that seem lit from inside, suspended and still; low mounds of soil with ceramics and flowers sit around the floor.
claims: Calls up ancestral knowledge and Kaqchikel Maya ceremony.
references: Kaqchikel Maya ceremony, San Juan Comalapa
works.photo_notes: Berlinartlink photo: stones in gauze above earth mounds.

works.title: We Rise By Lifting Others
works.medium_line: LED bulbs and Flex LED on a wooden structure
works.what_you_see: A festival-style light structure runs about 34 metres at the entrance, built like the lit arches of Italian saints' day parades.
claims: Message of collective uplift.
works.photo_notes: Design Pataki photo: lit arch.

works.title: "Untitled" (Go-Go Dancing Platform)
works.medium_line: light blue platform framed by bulbs; live dancer
works.what_you_see: A small light-blue platform framed by light bulbs. Once or twice a day a dancer in silver lamé briefs steps up and dances about five minutes to music only he hears.
nonvisual: sound: music on dancer's personal device, inaudible to the audience
claims: Made in grief after a partner and father died.
works.photo_notes: ARTnews photo.
